t: Maximum Alternating Subsequence Sum — Even/Odd State Machine DP
o: Choose any subsequence, reindex it from 0, and score it +,-,+,-,... by slot parity, maximizing the total; a single element is itself a valid subsequence occupying a plus slot. In Example 1, picking [4,2,5] scores (4+5)-2 = 7, beating the full array alternating sum of 4 because the trailing 3 can simply be skipped. In Example 2, the lone element [8] gives 8 — nothing forces us to pick the smaller values before it. In Example 3, [6,1,5] yields 6-1+5 = 10 by harvesting the valley at 1 between the peaks. With n up to 10^5, exponential enumeration is hopeless, yet a linear pass suffices once we notice only two states matter: whether the next picked element would land on a plus slot or a minus slot.
k: Only slot parity matters: track the best score of subsequences whose next element lands on a plus (+) slot versus a minus (-) slot.
Each value x offers exactly two transitions: enter a plus slot gaining odd + x, or enter a minus slot losing even - x.
The problem is Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II with a free opening purchase, so the answer also equals the sum of positive consecutive price gains starting from price 0.

a.i: Recursively decide include/skip for each element while tracking how many elements were taken so far; the taken count parity determines the sign. Take the maximum over both branches at every position. This is a direct translation of the statement and a useful correctness reference, but exponential time rules it out for large n.
s: Define dfs(i, cnt): best additional score using nums[i..] given cnt elements already taken.
Including gives sign * nums[i] + dfs(i + 1, cnt + 1) where sign is + for even cnt, - otherwise.
a.t: O(2^n) — every include/skip combination is explored

a.i: Maintain even = best alternating sum of a processed-prefix subsequence whose NEXT slot is plus-signed, and odd = best with next slot minus-signed; both start at 0 for the empty subsequence. Each new x updates even = max(even, odd + x) and odd = max(odd, even - x); reading the freshly updated even inside the same iteration only permits taking x twice (+x then -x), which nets zero and is harmless. The final answer is even, since ending on a plus slot is always at least as good as stopping earlier. This is the classic held/not-held stock DP in disguise.
s: For each x: even = max(even, odd + x).
a.sp: O(1) — two running variables replace the memo table

a.i: Interpret each -slot as buying and the following +slot as selling; the very first +slot is a sell after a free buy at price 0. Maximum profit with unlimited transactions equals the sum of all positive consecutive gains, so the answer is max(nums[0], 0) plus every positive difference nums[i] - nums[i-1]. Harvesting every ascending run corresponds exactly to picking peaks and valleys as the optimal subsequence, e.g. [6,2,1,2,4,5] collects 6 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 10.
s: For each i >= 1 add max(0, nums[i] - nums[i-1]) to ans.
a.t: O(n) — one pass of adjacent differences

w: Lead with the state-machine DP and offer the greedy as an elegant equivalence. Pitfalls: returning int in Java/C++ (values reach 10^5 * 10^5 / 2, so use long); forgetting a lone element is a legal subsequence; confusing slot parity with value alternation — equal values may occupy consecutive slots. Follow-ups: minimum alternating subsequence sum (negate the array), or variants constraining the subsequence length, which need an extra DP dimension.
